findings.finding: 1. The listener acceptance fails at the base only if the test goes through the listener's own option construction, and 'reports the connection lost' has three possible machine checks (Connected(), the log line, /healthz), of which /healthz already fails a silent cut today.
findings.answer: Plan section 2.2 fixes the observable as the `envoy nats disconnected` line (internal/bus/connect.go:245-250) for both client names, read from the real listener process started through listenerStreamOptions and openLiveTopics, bounded at 5 s so the base run fails fast. /healthz is rejected with its reason.

findings.finding: 2. Item 1.8 cannot observe 'this client's first reconnect-hook run' from cmd/dispatch without new internal/bus surface: the counters are unexported and a hook added after the constructor races the first connection event.
findings.answer: Plan section 3 names the seam (one exported read of hookedEvents under c.mu), requires a bus test that proves its meaning before the helper changes, keeps the reconcileFailure arm, and names the ConnectOption fallback and when to take it.

findings.finding: 3. 'What the pings cost at today's session count' has no client that scales with sessions and no named source for the count.
findings.answer: Plan section 2.3: the cost is per listener process (two connections, 1 ping/s each; one connection without ENVOY_SUBSCRIBE_ALL_TOPICS), it does not scale with sessions, the per-session TypeScript clients already ping at 10 s and are untouched, and today's count is read live with the envoy_sessions tool and quoted with its time.

findings.finding: 4. Acceptance 6 is machine-checkable only with a fixed per-item roll call; items 1.3, 1.5 and 1.6 are otherwise human-decidable.
findings.answer: Plan sections 1, 4.1 and 5 require a fourteen-line roll call in the body, each line `done <file:line>` or `not done: <reason>`; item 1.3's symbol list is fixed in the roll-call row, item 1.5's scope in section 4.4, item 1.6's in its row.

findings.finding: 5. Item 1.10's premise is false: packages/envoy/AGENTS.md has no Rollout paragraph; the wrong sentences are :40 and :2791, and :2790 is already correct.
findings.answer: The item's row in plan section 1 names AGENTS.md:40 and :2791, records that :2790 is already correct and that no Rollout paragraph exists, and keeps deploy/README.md:178-179 (true of the listener).

findings.finding: 6. Items 2.1-2.3 are in packages/envoy-client, not packages/claude-envoy, so Acceptance 6 names the wrong suite.
findings.answer: Plan section 0 fact 3 and the three rows give the real paths; section 5 adds the envoy-client and claude-envoy stall suites as the envoy-session-stall job runs them. Recorded as a spec departure.

findings.finding: 7. Item 1.1's correction is also owed to released CHANGELOG.md paragraphs, and item 1.9 has the same question.
findings.answer: Plan section 4.2: no CHANGELOG.md is edited (the repository's rule is that the fold writes it, and those entries record what shipped); the correction lands in the live docs and this pull request's fragment, and the roll call says so.

findings.finding: 8. Item 1.6 is already true in AGENTS.md:2785 and stream.go:215-217; what is missing is the send-order exception and the unqualified dedupe claim in publisher.go and the duplicate-window paragraph.
findings.answer: The item's row scopes it to async.go's Window doc, publisher.go (:100-101, :232-252, :246-248), AGENTS.md:1412-1420 and the window_test.go copy, and the roll call marks the already-true parts.

findings.finding: 9. Item 1.5 points at an off-repo review whose line numbers are stale, and folding across cmd/listener and cmd/dispatch needs shared test support.
findings.answer: Plan section 4.4 names the five sub-items at today's anchors, folds 9a, 9b and 9e into internal/bus/bustest with the bustest-imports-bus cycle stated, and names 9c and 9d not done with their reasons, which Acceptance 6 permits.

findings.finding: 10. Live work on main conflicts: #2504 touches four targets, #2404, #2461, #2508 others, and AGENTS.md is in thirty or more open pull requests.
findings.answer: Plan section 6 step 7 puts every AGENTS.md edit last, in one commit of smallest single-line replacements; section 7 records the conflict risk and the rule that the base comes in only on a real conflict.

findings.finding: 11. A one-second ping changes deployment behaviour: the listener's readiness gates its tailnet advertisement, and webhook_frozen_bus_test.go builds its bus by hand so it will not exercise the option.
findings.answer: Plan section 2.4 states both in the body: the trade with its evidence (connect.go:60-66's own caveat, Dispatch's precedent, /healthz already failing a cut inside 3 s), and the decision to leave webhook_frozen_bus_test.go as it is, named in the roll call.

findings.finding: 12. The daemon is named conditionally and the condition is false, so the outage's other blind client is silently left out.
findings.answer: Plan section 4.6: the daemon's client is out of this pull request (another module, not a client of this package), the body says so, and the planner reports the finding with its evidence and the one-line fix shape to the architect, which decides the scope.

findings.finding: 13. The outage diagnosis's own numbers (4 m 45 s, 'every publish was refused') are unverified here.
findings.answer: Plan section 4.7: the body attributes them to the diagnosis and claims no production measurement, while proving the mechanism from the code.

findings.finding: 14. Item 1.2's blast radius is four places beyond the item: two doc phrasings, the test row's doc, and the released CHANGELOG.
findings.answer: The item's row lists stream.go:500, keeper_test.go:293 and :280-282, stream.go:491-493 and keeper.go:121, names stream_config_test.go:331-335 as the test that keeps the guarantee, and leaves the released CHANGELOG under section 4.2.

findings.finding: 15. Item 1.4 is possible as written and unpinned by tests; its one other copy of '1 to 5' is cmd/dispatch/settings.go:83. Item 1.7 is wholly undone.
findings.answer: The 1.4 row takes the fold at render.go:270 only, and section 4.3 leaves settings.go:83 with its reason; the 1.7 row gives the architecture-doc row, the outcome list and the three new assertions.
